issues.message: Transitions leaving a pseudostate cannot have triggers (from choice).
entry of 'A': '1' is not allowed: the state machine has no variables, so use function calls like isReady() combined with !, && and ||.
exit of 'A': Dotted names are not allowed: use a single function name like doThing().
do of 'A': Actions cannot use !, && or ||: separate several calls with ;
Invariant of 'A': '>' is not allowed: the state machine has no variables, so use function calls like isReady() combined with !, && and ||.
Stereotype of 'A': '1bad' is not a valid name: use letters, digits and _ only, not starting with a digit.
Deferrable event of 'A': A time event cannot be deferred; use a named event.
Deferrable event of 'A': Events are plain names without (): write go.
Trigger: Change events (when) are not supported: use a named event or after(...).
Trigger: The time of an after() trigger must be greater than zero.
Guard: '>' is not allowed: the state machine has no variables, so use function calls like isReady() combined with !, && and ||.
Effect: Actions cannot use !, && or ||: separate several calls with ;
Guard: [else] is only allowed on transitions leaving a choice or junction.
Time triggers (after) can only be used on transitions leaving a state.
Duplicate id 's1'.
Duplicate id 'ep'.
Duplicate id 't1'.
Only composite states can have entry/exit points; add a region to 'Dup'.
A connection point reference must be placed on the border of a submachine state.
Only composite states can have entry/exit points; add a region to 'Dup'.
Connection points of the state machine need a name so submachine states can reference them.
A top-level region can contain at most one initial pseudostate.
History pseudostates are only meaningful inside a composite state.
'Comp' is entered by default but its region 'upper' has no initial pseudostate.
'Comp' is entered by default but its region has no initial pseudostate.
Another state named 'S' exists in the same region.
The transition leaving an initial pseudostate cannot have a guard.
A history pseudostate can have at most one outgoing (default) transition.
Transitions leaving entry point entry point must target a vertex inside 'Dup'.
The connection point reference does not refer to an entry or exit point of the submachine.
Transitions into entry reference connection point reference must come from outside 'S'.
Transitions leaving exit point exit point must target a vertex outside 'Comp'.
A fork must have exactly one incoming transition.
A fork must have at least two outgoing transitions.
Transitions leaving a fork cannot have guards or triggers.
A join must have at least two incoming transitions.
Transitions entering a join cannot have guards or triggers.
A final state cannot have outgoing transitions.
A terminate pseudostate cannot have outgoing transitions.
A junction must have at least one incoming transition.
Transitions leaving entry point entry point must target a vertex inside 'Dup'.
Entry point entry point of the state machine has no outgoing transition.
Exit point 'out' of the state machine cannot have outgoing transitions; the referencing submachine state continues from its connection point reference.
'Dup' has several completion transitions without triggers or guards.
'Dup' has several completion transitions without triggers or guards.
An internal transition must start and end on the same state.
'Dup' has several completion transitions without triggers or guards.
A local transition must go from a composite state to a vertex it contains.
'Dup' has several completion transitions without triggers or guards.
Comments cannot be connected by transitions.
Transition target 'nope' does not exist.
Transitions leaving a pseudostate cannot have triggers (from terminate).
Time triggers (after) can only be used on transitions leaving a state.
States of a protocol state machine cannot have entry/exit/do behaviors ('Open').
Protocol transitions cannot have effects.
